title: Longest Run of Equal Values
statement: You are given n integers in a row. A run is a block of equal values that sit next to each other. Find the length of the longest run. Equal values that are not side by side do not join. This is a common interview question on arrays.
inputFormat: The first line has n. The second line has n integers separated by spaces.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the length of the longest run of equal consecutive values.
explanations: The values 2 2 2 form the longest run. It has length 3. The runs of 1 and 3 are shorter.
The first 7 7 has length 2. The last 7 7 7 has length 3. The lone 1 splits the 7s, so the answer is 3.
reference:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
best = 1
cur = 1
for i in range(1, n):
    if a[i] == a[i - 1]:
        cur += 1
    else:
        cur = 1
    best = max(best, cur)
print(best)
